territorial_scope.description: Applies to taxpayers, energy utilities and projects in Indiana, under Indiana Code.

evidence.quote: a taxpayer's expenditures incurred in the manufacture of a small modular nuclear reactor in Indiana

summary.short: Indiana statute creating a 20% state tax credit for manufacturing small modular nuclear reactors, and new procedures before the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission for energy utility generation plans and large load customer projects, plus retirement-reporting amendments. Effective dates vary by section.
summary.long: The act adds IC 6-3.1-45, a tax credit equal to 20% of a taxpayer's qualified investment in manufacturing small modular nuclear reactors in Indiana, usable against adjusted gross income, financial institutions and insurance premiums taxes, with carryover, pass-through shareholder claims and no refund. It adds IC 8-1-7.9, letting energy utilities seek expedited Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission review of expedited generation resource (EGR) plans and of projects serving large load customers, defined by new demand, a capital investment above $500,000,000 and at least 50 full-time employees. Large load projects require customer reimbursement of at least 80% of allocable project costs, pre-filing meetings, and commission orders within 90 to 150 days; the commission may approve cost recovery with a return. It amends IC 8-1-8.5-2.1 to require notice to the commission of retirements of generation facilities of at least 80 megawatts (expiring July 1, 2026), and IC 8-1-8.5-13 to add reporting on planned retirements and refuelings, staff review, and commission orders directing acquisition or prohibiting retirement. Section 1 is effective January 1, 2025 (retroactive), Section 2 upon passage, Sections 3 and 4 on July 1, 2025.

enforcement.note: The text states no fines, criminal penalties, private damages or suspensions. Sec. 24(g) of IC 8-1-8.5-style chapter 7.9 (Sec. 24(g) of new IC 8-1-7.9) lets the commission modify or revoke an order approving a large-load project if completion is no longer in the public interest, after an investigation under IC 8-1-2-58 through IC 8-1-2-60, which are cross-referenced but not reproduced. This is recorded as regulatory control, not a sanction. Sec. 8(b) of IC 6-3.1-45 bars carryback or refund of unused credits, which is a limit on benefits, not a sanction.
